result.summary: Extracts nine P2P message handlers from PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage() in net_processing.cpp into dedicated private helper functions. Each handler (getaddr, getdata, getblocks, getheaders, inv, sendtxrcncl, tx, cmpctblock, and version) is moved in its own commit. A preparatory commit drops a __func__ prefix from a getheaders log, and a final commit cleans up formatting and local control flow.
result.problem: PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage() handles all P2P message types inline in a single monolithic function of roughly 1,500 lines, making message handling logic difficult to navigate and review.
evidence: Author notes the change follows the pattern of merged PRs extracting ProcessPong() and ProcessAddrs(), as suggested in PR #34588 review discussion
result.scope_notes: Diff is large (+1080/-1031) but structured as nine individual move-only commits between a preparatory logging commit and a cleanup commit, intended to be reviewed with git move-detection options.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased without changes to the overall structure or commit sequence.
result.card: Extracts handling logic for nine P2P message types from PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage() into dedicated helper functions in net_processing.cpp. The change breaks up a monolithic ~1,500-line message dispatch routine into separate handlers (getaddr, getdata, getblocks, getheaders, inv, sendtxrcncl, tx, cmpctblock, version) to improve readability and code navigation. The author cites reviewer guidance from PR #34588 and precedent from earlier extractions of pong and addrs message handlers. The PR consists of nine move-only extraction commits flanked by a preparatory log adjustment and a formatting cleanup commit.

risk.why: Unintended changes in control flow, locking annotations, or state updates during message extraction could introduce P2P message handling regressions or disconnects.
